findings.evidence: `Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowers/RatAlgebra.lean:249` declares `variable {R : Type*} [CommSemiring R]`, then adds `[Algebra ℚ R]` at line 260 for `dpow_eq_inv_fact_smul`; the PR's definitions and all results except lines 98 and 163 use no negation or subtraction.
findings.fix: Use `[Semiring A] [Algebra ℚ A]` globally (and `[Semiring B]` in `map_dividedPower`), add `[Ring A]` locally only to `dividedPower_neg` and `dividedPower_sub`, and weaken `dividedPower_eq_dpow` to `[CommSemiring R]`.
findings.issue: The global `[Ring A]` unnecessarily restricts every declaration, and line 174 similarly overstates `[CommRing R]`; Mathlib develops rational divided powers under `[CommSemiring R] [Algebra ℚ R]`.

summary: The module imposes `Ring`/`CommRing` globally although most divided-power operations naturally require only semirings; additive inverses are needed only for the negation and subtraction results.
